elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Replacement § 7.7 reads: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." This deletes the fifteen-percent-per-week liquidated damages charge in the original § 7.7 and states the blanket no-LD position in operative language, not merely in the comment.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind survives (§ 7.7 bars all such amounts; § 10 requires only payment for delivered work and § 27 permits termination without penalty), so there is no liquidated amount that could be other than an early-termination fee.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in the redlined text, so there is no amount requiring a three-month cap. The fallback cap is offered only in the margin comment as a negotiating alternative, which is appropriate since the preferred position is taken in the operative text.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — the blanket bar in the new § 7.7 means zero liquidated amounts are payable by Customer, which is at least as protective as confining them to a single early-termination fee.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is delivered by operative text in the replacement § 7.7, which both removes the offending Customer-payable liquidated damages and affirmatively confirms that none are payable.

Fallback elements are all vacuously met because the redline eliminates every Customer-payable liquidated amount; the three-month early-termination cap is correctly reserved to the comment as a fallback offer rather than inserted as an extra operative term.

Minimality holds: the change is confined to § 7.7, a single sentence, with no added survival tail, procedure, interest substitute, damages categories, or other boilerplate beyond the one checklist element.

Intent is preserved: Vendor's underlying payment entitlement and other remedies are untouched (Customer's obligation to pay invoices and § 10's payment-for-delivered-work mechanic survive), the edit introduces no undefined terms, and it does not contradict § 27's termination-without-penalty language. Drafter should confirm no other section cross-references § 7.7's former late-payment charge (e.g., a late-fee or suspension provision keyed to it) so no dangling reference remains.

Original clause was correctly classified as a deviation in walk-away territory: fifteen percent of annual Fees per week is uncapped, can exceed remaining contract value, is triggered by a minor breach (a ten-day late invoice), and is not an early-termination fee, so it fails the fallback on material terms.
